subject.title: [Feature]: Skill lifecycle management — auto-optimization on failure + usage-based retirement

question: Should OpenClaw own failure-driven skill repair and usage-based retirement in core, expose plugin/ClawHub APIs for it, or reject the lifecycle policy for now?
rationale: Current main only covers durable user-correction capture; the remaining request adds new inference policy, public config, persistence, and user-skill lifecycle behavior that automation should not choose alone.

options.title: Design Core/API Boundary
options.body: Keep this issue open as the canonical design item, split optimization and retirement into narrower maintainer-approved tracks, and decide what belongs in core versus plugin APIs.

options.title: Route To Plugin/ClawHub APIs
options.body: Treat the capability as external lifecycle tooling unless maintainers identify a missing core hook or state API that must be added first.

options.title: Close As Not Planned
options.body: Reject automatic repair and retirement policy if maintainers do not want OpenClaw to infer lifecycle actions from execution history.

recommendation.title: Design Core/API Boundary
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the canonical design item, split optimization and retirement into narrower maintainer-approved tracks, and decide what belongs in core versus plugin APIs.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter authored the recent default suggestion tier and explicitly scoped broader self-reflection as future work, making him the strongest product-direction owner in the inspected history.
